final_recommendation: The room converged on a coordinated rescue package: SNB provides 50bn liquidity facility with 16bn first-loss absorption, UBS commits to unconditional acquisition closing Monday, Federal Council co-signs capacity language, and a joint statement releases Friday 17:00 with Sunday evening operational confirmation. Settlement systems must display draws in real-time Monday 09:00 to prevent deposit panic.
minority_objections: Federal Council initially resisted open-ended backstop language, demanding hard ceiling and triggering mechanism to avoid blank-check perception
AT1 representative repeatedly demanded explicit exclusion language in facility agreement, not just public statement, to prevent creditor panic
key_conflicts: Federal Council vs SNB on Sunday statement language: SNB wanted 'additional capacity available' commitment, Federal Council insisted on 'capacity sufficient within agreed parameters' to avoid blank-check perception
UBS CEO vs regulators on AT1 conversion risk: demanded written guarantee of zero conversion triggers before committing to acquisition
Wealth client vs all parties on real-time systems visibility: insisted depositors must see liquidity draws live Monday 09:00 or assets move regardless of statements
key_concessions: SNB accepted 16bn loss ceiling (initially sought broader authority) to secure Federal Council political support
Federal Council agreed to co-sign Sunday statement despite political cost concerns, conditional on capped language
UBS CEO committed to unconditional acquisition after receiving written guarantee on loss perimeter and AT1 exclusion
FINMA revised Sunday statement language from 'if market conditions require' to 'to sustain depositor confidence' to signal commitment over rationing
red_lines: UBS: zero AT1 conversion or creditor loss-sharing post-close, or acquisition is off
Federal Council: no open-ended public backstop language that reads as blank check
AT1 representative: identical AT1 subordination language across all statements (Friday and Sunday) with no softening or caveats
Wealth client: real-time settlement visibility Monday 09:00 or assets move before market close
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Weekend communication vacuum: room focused on Friday statement release but only belatedly addressed how depositors would receive information between Friday 17:00 and Monday 09:00
Systems execution risk: real-time settlement visibility became critical constraint only in final rounds, not surfaced early as potential failure point
Deposit velocity uncertainty: CS CEO's 10-15bn estimate treated as reliable despite acknowledged messiness below top-20 clients; no scenario planning for 20-25bn outflow until Round 8-10

Creditor legal review timing: AT1 representative's concern that creditor lawyers would review facility agreement language over weekend was acknowledged but not fully addressed with concrete legal review process
downstream_risk_variables: Monday 09:00-10:00 deposit outflow velocity: if exceeds 15bn in first two hours, facility burns faster than planned
Settlement systems synchronization: any lag between SNB feed and CS account display triggers confidence collapse
Weekend media coverage: if statement lands Friday 17:00 but major outlets don't cover until Monday, depositors miss signal
Creditor lawyer interpretation: if facility agreement AT1 language differs from public statement, creditors move assets Monday regardless of statements
Federal Council political tolerance: if Monday outflow hits 20-25bn, political room for additional capacity announcement unclear
uncertainty_notes: The room locked a rescue structure but left critical execution dependencies unresolved: (1) whether CS's internal account systems will actually sync with SNB settlement feed by 09:15 Monday—only verbally confirmed, not tested; (2) whether 10-15bn deposit outflow estimate holds or undershoots reality; (3) whether Federal Council's Sunday statement language ('capacity sufficient within agreed parameters') will be read by markets as commitment or hedge; (4) what happens if facility burns through 30-40bn by Wednesday—no contingency beyond Federal Council's private calls to top depositors. The rescue is legally locked but operationally fragile.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: Federal Council R2: '16bn loss perimeter sits with UBS as acquirer and FINMA's resolution toolkit, not on our balance sheet'—liquidity facility alone insufficient, required acquisition + loss absorption structure
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS CEO R4: 'I'm in. Name me as buyer in the statement at 17:00—UBS commits to acquisition'—acquisition became the binding solution, not optional path
marker_evidence.government_support: SNB R3: '50bn emergency facility' + Federal Council R8 co-signature on Sunday statement—government liquidity and political backing were non-negotiable conditions of the rescue
marker_evidence.client_flight: CS CEO R2: 'depositors don't see concrete numbers before close of business, they're moving assets' + R7: '10-15bn walks Monday morning'—deposit flight drove the urgency and shaped facility sizing
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 rep R2-R10: repeatedly demanded explicit AT1 exclusion language in statements and facility agreement—raised as concern and secured protective language, but did not block or reshape the core deal terms
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 rep R3: 'does 16bn loss perimeter include any creditor conversion, AT1 write-down?'—conflict over who bears losses was raised and addressed with equity/subordinated debt language, but did not force a concession on deal structure
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: Federal Council R2 asked if resolution mechanics trigger 'creditor litigation that derails the whole deal'—single mention, SNB replied it was legally defensible, no further discussion or constraint imposed
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: Wealth client R2: 'I need to see the statement published before close of business' + FINMA R3: 'facility agreement by 16:15' + multiple references to Friday 17:00 deadline—time pressure to Friday close drove coordination mechanics and forced rapid lock-in of terms
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Federal Council R1: 'does it stop deposit flight over the weekend, or just delay panic until Monday?' + R10 focus on Monday 09:00 settlement visibility—Monday risk was acknowledged as background concern but did not drive a specific decision or number; the room's concrete actions targeted Friday statement release and Sunday confirmation
